The Intriguing Contribution of
Hippocampal Long-Term Depression
to Spatial Learning and Long-Term
Memory
Martin Stacho and Denise Manahan-Vaughan *
Department of Neurophysiology, Medical Faculty, Ruhr University Bochum, Bochum, Germany
Long-term potentiation (LTP) and long-term depression (LTD) comprise the principal
cellular mechanisms that fulﬁll established criteria for the physiological correlates of
learning and memory. Traditionally LTP , that increases synaptic weights, has been
ascribed a prominent role in learning and memory whereas LTD, that decreases them,
has often been relegated to the category of “counterpart to LTP” that serves to prevent
saturation of synapses. In contradiction of these assumptions, studies over the last
several years have provided functional evidence for distinct roles of LTD in speciﬁc
aspects of hippocampus-dependent associative learning and information encoding.
Furthermore, evidence of the experience-dependent “pruning” of excitatory synapses,
the majority of which are located on dendritic spines, by means of LTD has been
provided. In addition, reports exist of the temporal and physical restriction of LTP in
dendritic compartments by means of LTD. Here, we discuss the role of LTD and LTP in
experience-dependent information encoding based on empirical evidence deriv…

{"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=How+does+path-dependent+sequential+reinforcement+learning+contribute+to+the+emergence+and+stabilization+of+agent+preferences%3F&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.70675/8cc458a7ze8a6z4521z93b8z789b13bbf0bc\", \"title\": [\"Protocol emergence with multi-agent reinforcement learning\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:title>Émergence de protocoles avec apprentissage par renforcement multi-agents</jats:title>\\n                <jats:p xml:lang=\\\"fr\\\">Dans ce travail, nous introduisons une nouvelle technique automatisée de conception de protocoles appelée émergence de protocole. Dans le contexte de l'émergence de protocole, les nœuds du réseau échangent des messages de contrôle pour coordonner la livraison de données à travers le réseau, le tout sans accord préalable sur la signification de ces messages. Cette approche peut être considérée comme une technique combinée de signalisation et d'optimisation de réseau. L'émergence de protocole offre la possibilité de minimiser les surcharges de signalisation, particulièrement adaptée aux scénarios de communication massive de type machine (MMTC), et facilite la création de protocoles personnalisés adaptés à des applications spécifiques. Cette adaptabilité est particulièrement bénéfique dans des environnements relativement stables, tels que des installations industrielles intérieures. Pour commencer, nous présentons les concepts fondamentaux de l'émergence de protocole en introduisant un cadre. Ce cadre décrit des méthodes pour évaluer les performances des protocoles, caractériser les protocoles, coordonner entre les nœuds et interpréter les messages échangés. Nous analysons ce cadre dans le contexte d'un problème d'accès multiple entrelacé. Dans la partie suivante de ce travail, nous évaluons les performances de l'émergence de protocole dans un scénario impliquant une allocation de ressources contiguë. Cette évaluation vise à comprendre les capacités d'apprentissage et les limitations de l'émergence de protocole, démontrant sa robustesse à certains paramètres et abordant les défis liés à la scalabilité des équipements utilisateur (UE), par exemple. {"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=failure+modes+of+instruction-following+in+AI+systems+when+human+objectives+are+contextually+inadequate&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.7433399\", \"title\": [\"When Agentic AI Breaks Software Quality Assurance: Failure Modes, Reliability Risks, and Governance Strategies for Autonomous Testing Systems\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>The emergence of agentic artificial intelligence (AI) is changing software quality assurance from a predominantly human-directed activity into an increasingly autonomous process in which AI systems can generate tests, execute programs, interpret failures, modify test suites, and iteratively refine their actions. While these capabilities promise substantial improvements in testing speed, coverage, and engineering productivity, they also introduce a distinct class of quality risks. An autonomous testing agent can produce a technically executable test that encodes an incorrect assumption, misinterpret a failure, optimize for coverage rather than meaningful defect detection, or repeatedly reinforce an erroneous testing strategy. This article examines these risks through an integrative review of research on large language models (LLMs), automated software testing, AI-assisted software engineering, and AI governance. The analysis identifies six interconnected failure modes: erroneous test generation, defective test oracles, autonomous error propagation, coverage-driven quality illusion, contextual and repository misunderstanding, and governance and accountability failure. The article argues that the central challenge is not simply whether AI can generate valid tests, but whether autonomous testing systems can maintain trustworthy quality judgments under uncertainty. Drawing on empirical evidence from recent studies of ChatGPT, LLM-based test generation, TestGen-LLM, and software-engineering agents, the article proposes a risk-based governance model built around bounded autonomy, independent verification, traceability, human checkpoints, continuous monitoring, and explicit escalation mechanisms.
